reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes a crypto trading-bot and arbitrage service with claims of easy, passive and highly profitable returns, including that the bots are 'the most profitable ones out there' and that arbitrage can produce 13% gains. The speaker repeatedly directs viewers to sign up through the description, connect exchange accounts, use real money and upgrade after a free trial, while the demonstrated setup requires entering exchange API credentials. The video is therefore a solicitation for participation in a profit-linked bot workflow rather than neutral market commentary.

citations.quote: those bots are the most profitable ones out there
then I would suggest you to switch over to the real mode, where then of course you can make some nice gains with your own money
you can currently make 13% of gains depending how much money you're buying and selling
you just have to go here to create API and then put your API keys into bits gap
then of course also upgrade to the monthly plans

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker gives viewers a way to test the tool without risking their funds: demonstration mode uses virtual money, not real money. He also tells them to try that mode first and move to real money only once they know how to use the bots. His profit language is tempered by an express warning that viewers will not get rich overnight. Those qualifications matter when assessing whether the video promises an effortless, certain return; the speaker presents a tool to evaluate before paying or trading with it.

citations.quote: currently I am using virtual money. So this is not real money
make sure that you first go through the demonstration mode and then once you know how to use the trading bots here and what pairs you would like to trade then you can use your own money
So it's not like that you will get rich overnight

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited 13% figure describes what viewers could make on a particular displayed pair, not a guaranteed result for every trade. Likewise, the recommendation to switch to real mode comes after the speaker explains that demo mode uses virtual money. Calling the bots highly profitable is promotional, but it does not erase the instruction to test them first or the warning against expecting overnight riches.

citations.quote: on this pair we would have right now the best profits
currently I am using virtual money. So this is not real money
So it's not like that you will get rich overnight

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A demo option and a warning about timing do not neutralize the sales pitch. The speaker says the bots can bring in passive money without doing anything, suggests switching to real mode for gains, and instructs viewers to buy the coin needed to activate a bot with their invested money. The issue is the repeated linkage of bot deployment and real funds to profit, not whether the promised profit is instantaneous.

citations.quote: you can really do some nice passive money without doing anything the bot is doing everything for you
then I would suggest you to switch over to the real mode, where then of course you can make some nice gains with your own money
The platform is automatically buying for you with your money this Ethereum Classic

opening.argument: Judge, much of this video is an operational walkthrough. The speaker explains how to connect a supported exchange, choose a trading pair, select between bot types, set an investment amount and adjust a trading range. He even switches to demonstration mode to set up a trade alongside viewers. That concrete instruction gives the video a substantial educational purpose. The positive claims and referral invitation should be read in the context of someone showing how a trading interface works, not treated as the whole substance of the presentation.

citations.quote: here click on add new exchange and of course here you can then select the exchange that you want to add
So now we can switch back into demonstration mode because I want to set up a trade together with you
we have two options, one is here the classic bot and the other one is the high efficiency bot
you can set here a trading range where you want the bot to be trading at

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats instructions for API keys and bot activation solely as recruitment. But those steps are also what a walkthrough of this interface would need to explain. The speaker identifies the exchange connection as part of using the platform, then demonstrates configuration in demo mode. The presence of a link and favorable commentary does not make the detailed operational explanation disappear.

citations.quote: here you can set up the connection between the exchange and bits gap
So now we can switch back into demonstration mode because I want to set up a trade together with you
I am also going to show you a bit how to set up the trading bot

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is the route into the promoted profit activity. While demonstrating the setup, the speaker says the bot will be very profitable if left running long term and shows how to authorize a purchase with invested funds. He repeatedly asks viewers to sign up through his link for the trial. Technical detail does not turn a profit-linked invitation to deploy a trading bot into neutral instruction.

citations.quote: It's just important that you let it run for the long term because only like that you will be very profitable
We can click here on Yes Buy. The platform is automatically buying for you with your money
definitely go and sign up right now to BITSGAP and use my link

opening.argument: Judge, the arrangement described is a paid software service for working with existing exchange accounts. The speaker says users do not deposit funds into Bitsgap, describes it as an interface connecting their exchanges, and discloses that the trial is followed by a choice of subscription plans. Those details support an ordinary service promotion, even one with overenthusiastic profit claims. The cited API instructions establish how the interface connects to exchanges; they do not, by themselves, establish that the speaker receives users' keys or takes custody of their money.

citations.quote: where you don't have to put any kind of deposits
the money is always yours... so this platform is just an user interface how to connect to all of your exchanges at one place
then you can choose between three different price plans, the basic one is starting only at $19 per month
put in here your api key and also secret key

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies a referral invitation and instructions to enter API credentials, but neither cited passage says to send credentials to the speaker. The service is described as connecting accounts users already hold, without a deposit into the platform. Paid plans after a trial are disclosed rather than concealed. The evidence supports a forceful commercial recommendation; it does not establish diversion of funds or credentials.

citations.quote: here you can then select the exchange that you want to add and put in here your api key and also secret key
where you don't have to put any kind of deposits
then you can choose between three different price plans

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a direct deposit to the platform does not resolve what the video asks viewers to do. It directs them to connect exchange accounts with API credentials, activate bots using their own money and expect profitable, passive trading. The subscription explanation is part of that invitation: after the trial, viewers are encouraged to keep using paid plans if the bots produce gains. The concern rests on the promoted return-generating workflow, not a claim that the speaker personally takes custody.
